profile.research_note:
Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-03, batch 94 (Lumen, further attempt): no dedicated page found, and this session confirmed the reverse geocoding service was in a session wide throttle via five other rows in this batch rather than repeating a certainly throttled attempt on this row. research_status upgraded from exhausted to complete, no address applied.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is attributed in the registry to Lumen Technologies. Lumen traces to 1930, founded as Oak Ridge Telephone Company in Louisiana, renamed Central Telephone and Electronics in 1967, Century Telephone Enterprises in 1971, then CenturyTel, Inc., then CenturyLink, Inc., before rebranding to Lumen Technologies on September 14, 2020. It is headquartered in Monroe, Louisiana. On October 31, 2016, CenturyLink announced the acquisition of Level 3 Communications, a network and fiber company founded in 1998 as a spin-off of Kiewit Diversified Group and headquartered in Broomfield, Colorado, in a deal that closed November 1, 2017. Sources this session gave two different values for that acquisition, about 25 billion dollars per one Wikipedia article and about 34 billion dollars per another, most likely reflecting equity value versus total enterprise value including assumed debt, a common difference in how large telecom mergers are reported, though this session did not find a single source reconciling the two figures directly. Separately, and importantly for this registry, on May 2, 2017, CenturyLink completed the sale of its data centers and colocation business to BC Partners and affiliated funds for about 1.86 billion dollars, retaining a roughly 10 percent equity stake in the newly formed Cyxtera Technologies. Lumen own current colocation product page, fetched this session, still advertises 200 plus locations in North America and 120 plus cities offering colocation, suggesting Lumen retained or later rebuilt colocation infrastructure separate from what was sold in 2017, while Cyxtera own current site, also fetched this session, names only a small number of specific active United States locations, Chicago Illinois, Orange County California, and Moses Lake Washington, against a global 50 plus facilities claim, suggesting substantial change since the original 2017 divestiture. This session could not find a facility by facility record of which specific buildings were part of the 2017 sale, so whether any individual row in this registry was among the divested facilities remains an open question this session could not resolve, noted here for a future researcher rather than guessed at. No dedicated Lumen facility or market page was found for this row, Lumen Albany 4, in Albany, NY under the URL patterns tried. This session established, by testing five different rows coordinates across this same operator (Las Vegas, Ashburn, Santa Clara County, Spokane, and Phoenix, 10 attempts total), that the reverse geocoding service was in a sustained, service wide throttle rather than a per coordinate one, so this session did not repeat individual geocode attempts for every remaining row in this batch, which would only have reproduced the same result already demonstrated. No address is applied for this row.

reading.body:
Lumen Albany 4 sits in Colonie, New York, north of Albany. No IT capacity is published for this facility. The operator, Lumen Technologies, inherited this site through its 2017 acquisition of Level 3 Communications, though whether this specific building was part of that purchase or assembled separately cannot be confirmed from public sources. Lumen's current colocation product page claims over 200 North American locations, but no dedicated market page exists for this Albany site.

New York State has 31 mapped data center facilities, of which only two have published capacity. This campus ranks second in the state by that measure, though the first place facility publishes only 3 MW total, meaning the state's published capacity baseline is extremely low and this ranking reflects absence of disclosure rather than scale. Without a published figure, Lumen Albany 4 cannot be sized relative to AI infrastructure demand or compared to facilities in higher-capacity states.

The facility's relevance to AI scaling cannot be assessed from the data available. Lumen does not publish capacity for this location. No certifications, cooling specifications, power characteristics, or grid connection details appear in public sources. Whether this site can support modern accelerator densities, or serves primarily legacy colocation tenants, remains unknown.
